components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.hanzi: 这件事由市场部主管负责。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yóu shìchǎngbù zhǔguǎn fùzé.
example.english: This matter is handled by the marketing department manager.
example.fact: 主管 works as both a noun ("the person in charge, a supervisor") and a verb ("to be in charge of," 主管财务 "to be in charge of finances") — the same flexible pattern as English "head" ("the department head" vs. "to head the department").

examples.hanzi: 请联系销售主管，他会给你答复。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng liánxì xiāoshòu zhǔguǎn, tā huì gěi nǐ dáfù.
examples.english: Please contact the sales supervisor; he will give you a reply.

examples.hanzi: 这个部门的主管明天出差。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bùmén de zhǔguǎn míngtiān chūchāi.
examples.english: The head of this department is on a business trip tomorrow.

components.note: 刂 (knife; 刀) — marks cutting, as in 别 separate, 刻 carve, 划 slice; 刮 is scraping, shaving or blowing wind.
舌 (shé) — loose sound hint (guā vs shé).

example.hanzi: 外面刮大风了。
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn guā dàfēng le.
example.english: It's very windy outside.
example.fact: 刮 is to scrape, shave, or blow: 刮风 (the wind blows), 刮胡子 (shave), 刮痧 (gua sha, a scraping therapy). The idiom 刮目相看 means to look at someone with new eyes.

examples.hanzi: 他每天早上刮胡子。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang guā húzi.
examples.english: He shaves every morning.

examples.hanzi: 台风刮倒了很多树。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng guā dǎo le hěn duō shù.
examples.english: The typhoon blew down many trees.

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
义 (justice, meaning) also lends its sound to 议 yì discuss, 仪 yí ceremony and 蚁 yǐ ant — a useful clue in many characters.

example.hanzi: 他是一个理想主义者。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè lǐxiǎng zhǔyìzhě.
example.english: He is an idealist.
example.fact: 主义 is Chinese's standard suffix for translating the Western "-ism" (社会主义 "socialism," 现实主义 "realism"), literally "guiding principle" from 主 ("master, lord") + 义 ("righteousness, doctrine") — one of the most productive loan-translation patterns in modern Chinese, coined largely through 19th/20th-century contact with Japanese kanji compounds.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个资本主义国家。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge zīběn zhǔyì guójiā.
examples.english: This is a capitalist country.

examples.hanzi: 她是一个乐观主义者。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge lèguān zhǔyìzhě.
examples.english: She is an optimist.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (silk), as in 红, 给; colours come from dyed silk.
录 (lù) — same sound — 绿 is lù (lǜ in colour), like 录.

example.hanzi: 春天来了,树叶都变绿了。
example.pinyin: Chūntiān lái le, shùyè dōu biàn lǜ le.
example.english: Spring has come and the leaves have turned green.
example.fact: 绿 is green: 绿色, 绿灯 (green light), 绿茶 (green tea). It carries a famous cultural twist: 戴绿帽子 ('wear a green hat') means to have an unfaithful partner, so avoid giving green hats. It is read lù in 绿林 and 鸭绿江 (the Yalu River).

examples.hanzi: 这家公司很重视绿色环保。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī hěn zhòngshì lǜsè huánbǎo.
examples.english: This company puts great emphasis on green environmental protection.

examples.hanzi: 红灯停,绿灯行。
examples.pinyin: Hóngdēng tíng, lǜdēng xíng.
examples.english: Red light stop, green light go.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.
巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.

example.hanzi: 我们常常一起去公园散步。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen chángcháng yìqǐ qù gōngyuán sànbù.
example.english: We often go to the park together to take walks.
example.fact: 常常 is simply 常 ("usual, often") reduplicated, functioning as an adverb of frequency close to 经常 — but unlike 经常, which can occasionally modify a noun in formal contexts, 常常 sits almost exclusively right before a verb, a subtle difference between two very close synonyms.

examples.hanzi: 我们周末常常去爬山。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò chángcháng qù pá shān.
examples.english: We often go hiking on the weekends.

examples.hanzi: 他常常忘记带钥匙。
examples.pinyin: Tā chángcháng wàngjì dài yàoshi.
examples.english: He often forgets to bring his keys.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 摄 is taking hold, then capturing on camera, as in 拍摄.
彡 (strokes of light or hair) — shining or decoration, as in 形 shape, 彩 colour, 须 beard.
景 (jǐng) is a close sound clue for yǐng; 景 itself meant light; 影 is its shadow.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.hanzi: 这位摄影师拍的婚纱照非常漂亮。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi shèyǐngshī pāi de hūnshā zhào fēicháng piàoliang.
example.english: The wedding photos this photographer took are very beautiful.
example.fact: 摄影师 stacks three meaningful pieces — 摄 ("to capture"), 影 ("shadow, image," built on 彡 "fine lines" for light and shadow), and the suffix 师 ("master, skilled professional") — literally "a master of capturing images," the same 师 that turns 工程 into "engineer" or plain 老 into "teacher."

examples.hanzi: 这位摄影师经常去世界各地旅行拍照。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi shèyǐngshī jīngcháng qù shìjiè gèdì lǚxíng pāizhào.
examples.english: This photographer often travels around the world taking photos.

examples.hanzi: 我哥哥想当一名摄影师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge xiǎng dāng yì míng shèyǐngshī.
examples.english: My older brother wants to be a photographer.

components.note: 营 (yíng) — camp, to run a business; as a part it sounds out 荧 yíng, 萤 yíng and 莹 yíng.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.

example.hanzi: 我们在山脚下的营地过了一夜。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài shānjiǎo xià de yíngdì guòle yí yè.
example.english: We spent a night at the campsite at the foot of the mountain.
example.fact: 营 originally referred to a military camp or barracks — where troops were quartered — and 营地 only broadened beyond that strictly military root to cover recreational or refugee camps (夏令营 "summer camp," 难民营 "refugee camp") in more modern usage.

examples.hanzi: 夏天，孩子们去山里的营地参加活动。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān, háizimen qù shān lǐ de yíngdì cānjiā huódòng.
examples.english: In summer, the kids go to a camp in the mountains for activities.

examples.hanzi: 军队在河边建立了一个临时营地。
examples.pinyin: Jūnduì zài hé biān jiànlì le yí ge línshí yíngdì.
examples.english: The army set up a temporary camp by the river.

components.note: 火 (fire) — marks fire and heat, as in 烧 burn, 灯 lamp, 烟 smoke; 煮 is boiling or cooking.
者 (zhě) — close sound: 煮 zhǔ. 者 also sounds out 猪 zhū and 著 zhù.

example.hanzi: 我在煮面条。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài zhǔ miàntiáo.
example.english: I'm cooking noodles.
example.fact: 煮 is cooking in water: 煮饭, 煮面, 煮鸡蛋. Cooking methods are distinct in Chinese: 煮 boil, 炒 stir-fry, 蒸 steam. 煮豆燃萁, 'burning bean stalks to cook beans', is an idiom for family members harming one another.

examples.hanzi: 请把鸡蛋煮五分钟。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ jīdàn zhǔ wǔ fēnzhōng.
examples.english: Please boil the eggs for five minutes.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈煮的汤很好喝。
examples.pinyin: Māma zhǔ de tāng hěn hǎohē.
examples.english: The soup Mom cooks is delicious.

components.note: 手 (hand) — the hand family: 打, 拿, 拉. 承 is usually explained as hands lifting something, to bear or accept (承认 admit, 承诺 promise).
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱; 担 is to carry on the shoulder, then to bear a duty.
旦 (dàn) is a close sound clue for dān; 旦 also sounds out 但 dàn and 胆 dǎn.

example.hanzi: 公司必须承担这次事故的责任。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī bìxū chéngdān zhè cì shìgù de zérèn.
example.english: The company must bear responsibility for this accident.
example.fact: 承 alone pictures multiple hands lifting something from below, and 担 (hand radical 扌 + phonetic 旦) relates to carrying a load, often on a shoulder pole — 承担 layers two separate "carrying" images into one verb for taking on a duty or responsibility.

examples.hanzi: 这个责任我愿意承担。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zérèn wǒ yuànyì chéngdān.
examples.english: I'm willing to take on this responsibility.

examples.hanzi: 他承担了这次活动的所有费用。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngdān le zhè cì huódòng de suǒyǒu fèiyòng.
examples.english: He covered all the costs of this event.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 挥 is to wave or wield.
军 (jūn) — near sound — 挥 is huī; 军 also sounds out 辉 huī.
宀 (roof) — a public building where officials work; 官 is an official.
官 (guān) gives the sound of 管 guǎn, 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.hanzi: 指挥官下令全体撤退。
example.pinyin: Zhǐhuīguān xiàlìng quántǐ chètuì.
example.english: The commander ordered a full retreat.
example.fact: 指挥官 adds the suffix 官 ("officer, official") onto 指挥 ("to direct, command," literally 指 "to point" + 挥 "to wave," the gestures of someone directing troops) — 指挥 alone already stands as a verb for "to conduct/direct," including conducting an orchestra (指挥乐队), while 官 narrows it specifically to a military commander.

examples.hanzi: 指挥官正在查看地图。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐhuīguān zhèngzài chákàn dìtú.
examples.english: The commander is looking at the map.

examples.hanzi: 飞行员接到了指挥官的命令。
examples.pinyin: Fēixíngyuán jiēdào le zhǐhuīguān de mìnglìng.
examples.english: The pilot received the commander's order.

components.note: 凶 (ominous) — an open pit 凵 with crossed marks inside: a trap, a sign of danger; seen in 凶手 murderer, 凶器 weapon.

example.hanzi: 那只狗很凶。
example.pinyin: Nà zhī gǒu hěn xiōng.
example.english: That dog is fierce.
example.fact: 凶 means fierce, or unlucky: 凶手 (murderer), 吉凶 (good or bad fortune), 他很凶 (he is harsh). Beware the homophones 兄 (older brother) and 胸 (chest).

examples.hanzi: 他今天特别凶,大家都不敢说话。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān tèbié xiōng, dàjiā dōu bù gǎn shuōhuà.
examples.english: He is especially fierce today; nobody dares to speak.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在找凶手。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài zhǎo xiōngshǒu.
examples.english: The police are looking for the killer.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
厂 (shelter) — 厂 here stands for a building; the traditional 廳 had 广, a wide hall.
丁 (dīng) — near sound — 厅 is tīng; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng and 顶 dǐng.

example.hanzi: 酒店大厅装饰得很豪华。
example.pinyin: Jiǔdiàn dàtīng zhuāngshì de hěn háohuá.
example.english: The hotel lobby is decorated very luxuriously.
example.fact: 厅 (building radical 广 + phonetic 丁) already means "a large room, hall" by itself — 大厅 simply reinforces that with 大 ("big"), producing a grander, more emphatic word for a hall or lobby, similar to how English sometimes says "great hall" for emphasis rather than just "hall."

examples.hanzi: 我们在酒店大厅等你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài jiǔdiàn dàtīng děng nǐ.
examples.english: We'll wait for you in the hotel lobby.

examples.hanzi: 会议在二楼的大厅举行。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì zài èr lóu de dàtīng jǔxíng.
examples.english: The meeting is held in the hall on the second floor.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 那条路经常出事,大家开车要小心。
example.pinyin: Nà tiáo lù jīngcháng chūshì, dàjiā kāichē yào xiǎoxīn.
example.english: Accidents often happen on that road, so everyone should drive carefully.
example.fact: 出事 is a verb-object compound (出 "to emerge, happen" + 事 "matter, incident") that's already grammatically complete, so it can't take a further direct object — "to have a car accident" needs the separate phrase 出车祸 rather than stacking a new object onto 出事.

examples.hanzi: 昨天晚上路口出事了，现在还在堵车。
examples.pinyin: Zuótiān wǎnshang lùkǒu chūshì le, xiànzài hái zài dǔ chē.
examples.english: There was an accident at the intersection last night, and traffic is still jammed.

examples.hanzi: 快打电话给他，我怕他出事了。
examples.pinyin: Kuài dǎ diànhuà gěi tā, wǒ pà tā chūshì le.
examples.english: Call him quickly; I'm afraid something happened to him.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand; 扫 (simplified 掃) is a hand with a broom 帚, to sweep.

example.hanzi: 周末我们一起打扫房间。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen yìqǐ dǎsǎo fángjiān.
example.english: On the weekend we clean the room together.
example.fact: 打扫 pairs 打 — a nearly meaningless "light verb" that shows up in many compound verbs, like 打电话 ("to phone") or 打篮球 ("to play basketball") — with 扫 ("to sweep," hand radical 扌 + 帚, a picture of a hand-held broom); 打 here contributes little beyond turning 扫 into a smoother two-syllable verb.

examples.hanzi: 我每天早上先打扫厨房。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang xiān dǎsǎo chúfáng.
examples.english: Every morning I clean the kitchen first.

examples.hanzi: 请把院子里的落叶打扫一下。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yuànzi lǐ de luòyè dǎsǎo yíxià.
examples.english: Please sweep up the fallen leaves in the yard.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — the bottom part, as in 布, 帽, 带. 希 is often read as a loosely woven cloth, so 'sparse, rare'; 希望 hope is a later extension.
乂 (crisscross) — Memory aid: crossed threads in an open weave 乂 on cloth 巾 — thin, rare, something you hope for.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — marks meat and the body, as in 脸, 腿; 腊 is dried or preserved meat.
昔 (xī) is a loose hint for là; 借 jiè and 错 cuò share it.

example.hanzi: 希腊有很多美丽的岛屿。
example.pinyin: Xīlà yǒu hěnduō měilì de dǎoyǔ.
example.english: Greece has many beautiful islands.
example.fact: The Antikythera mechanism, recovered from a Greek shipwreck in 1901, is a hand-cranked bronze device built around 150-100 BC that could predict eclipses and track the positions of the sun, moon, and planets. Its gearing is so sophisticated that historians consider it the world's oldest known analog computer, and nothing as complex reappeared in Europe for over a thousand years.

examples.hanzi: 我明年夏天想去希腊旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngnián xiàtiān xiǎng qù Xīlà lǚxíng.
examples.english: I want to travel to Greece next summer.

examples.hanzi: 你去过希腊吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ qùguo Xīlà ma?
examples.english: Have you ever been to Greece?

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and flowers, as in 草, 茶, 菜; 花 is a flower.
化 (huà) hints at the sound: 花 huā is close, and 化 also gives 华 huá and 货 huò.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国 country, 回 return, 图 map; 园 is a fenced garden.
元 (yuán) sounds exactly like 园; also in 远 yuǎn, 院 yuàn, 完 wán.

example.hanzi: 我们家后面有一个小花园。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā hòumiàn yǒu yígè xiǎo huāyuán.
example.english: There's a small garden behind our house.
example.fact: The Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew, in London, maintain living specimens of roughly one in every eight known plant species on Earth, making it one of the most complete plant collections anywhere. Its seed bank separately stores samples from over 10% of the world's wild plant species as insurance against extinction.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在花园里玩。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài huāyuán lǐ wán.
examples.english: The children are playing in the garden.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶喜欢在花园里种花。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai xǐhuan zài huāyuán lǐ zhòng huā.
examples.english: Grandma likes planting flowers in the garden.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — the outer box, as in 国 country and 回. The dictionary reading: four walls of a room, with a child (儿) inside; memory aid only, sound-borrowed.
儿 (legs/child) — inside the box, as in 先 and 兄. Memory aid: the shape is simply a box with two legs; it does not explain 'four'.
夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.

example.hanzi: 他四处寻找丢失的钥匙。
example.pinyin: Tā sìchù xúnzhǎo diūshī de yàoshi.
example.english: He searched everywhere for his lost keys.
example.fact: The pin-tumbler lock, still the most common design protecting doors worldwide, was patented by Linus Yale Jr. in 1861. Its core idea — a set of spring-loaded pins that must all be raised to exactly the right height by a matching key — has barely changed in over 160 years.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在院子里四处乱跑。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài yuànzi lǐ sìchù luàn pǎo.
examples.english: The kids are running around all over the yard.

examples.hanzi: 他四处打听这件事。
examples.pinyin: Tā sìchù dǎting zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: He asked around everywhere about this matter.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and agreements, as in 说, 请, 计; 订 is to book or settle by word.
丁 (dīng) hints at the sound: 订 dìng is close, as in 钉 dīng and 顶 dǐng.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
昏 (hūn, dusk) gives the exact sound; weddings were traditionally held at dusk, so the sound clue is also a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 他们上个月订婚了。
example.pinyin: Tāmen shàng gè yuè dìnghūn le.
example.english: They got engaged last month.
example.fact: The now-standard idea of a diamond engagement ring owes much to a 1947 De Beers advertising campaign built around the slogan 'A Diamond Is Forever.' Before that campaign, diamonds were just one option among many for engagement jewelry; afterward, they became the expected default across much of the Western world.

examples.hanzi: 他们打算明年订婚。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen dǎsuàn míngnián dìnghūn.
examples.english: They plan to get engaged next year.

examples.hanzi: 她去年和男朋友订婚了。
examples.pinyin: Tā qùnián hé nánpéngyou dìnghūn le.
examples.english: She got engaged to her boyfriend last year.

components.note: 缶 (clay jar) — marks pots and jars, as in 罐 jar, 缸 vat; a chipped jar is 缺, lacking.
夬 (guài/jué) is a loose hint for quē; 决 jué and 快 kuài share it.

example.hanzi: 这里缺水。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ quē shuǐ.
example.english: There is a shortage of water here.
example.fact: 缺 is to lack: 缺少 (be short of), 缺点 (shortcoming, the opposite of 优点), 缺席 (to be absent), 缺钱 (short of money). 缺德 literally 'lack virtue' means mean or immoral.

examples.hanzi: 我们还缺一个人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen hái quē yí ge rén.
examples.english: We still need one more person.

examples.hanzi: 他上课从不缺席。
examples.pinyin: Tā shàngkè cóng bù quēxí.
examples.english: He never misses class.

components.note: 氺 (water, a variant of 水) — the old form has water below hands and a big person above: calm, great, secure. Same character in 泰国 Thailand.
大 (big) — top of the character. Memory aid: a big (大) volume of water held steady is calm and 'great'.

example.hanzi: 我去年去了泰国。
example.pinyin: Wǒ qùnián qù le Tàiguó.
example.english: I went to Thailand last year.
example.fact: 泰 means peaceful: 泰然 (calm), 国泰民安 ('the country is at peace, the people safe'). It shortens 泰国 (Thailand), and 泰山 is the sacred Mount Tai, which is also a polite term for one's father-in-law.

examples.hanzi: 泰山是中国有名的山。
examples.pinyin: Tàishān shì Zhōngguó yǒumíng de shān.
examples.english: Mount Tai is a famous mountain in China.

examples.hanzi: 他很泰然,一点也不紧张。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn tàirán, yìdiǎn yě bù jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: He is calm and not nervous at all.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 拆 is taking apart with the hands.
斥 (chì) — loose sound hint (chāi vs chì).

example.hanzi: 他把旧房子拆了。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ jiù fángzi chāi le.
example.english: He tore down the old house.
example.fact: 拆 is to take apart or demolish: 拆开 (unwrap, open up), 拆除 (remove), 拆迁 (demolish and relocate, common in urban development), 拆礼物 (unwrap gifts). 拆台 means to sabotage someone's efforts.

examples.hanzi: 他把新买的玩具拆开了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ xīn mǎi de wánjù chāi kāi le.
examples.english: He unwrapped the new toy.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我拆一下这个包裹。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ chāi yíxià zhège bāoguǒ.
examples.english: Please help me open this package.

components.note: 術 (traditional) — 行 (road) plus 朮 (zhú) as sound: art, method. 术 is the sound part alone; same sound in 述 shù, as in 手术, 技术, 艺术.

example.hanzi: 他做了一个手术。
example.pinyin: Tā zuò le yí gè shǒushù.
example.english: He had an operation.
example.fact: 术 means skill or technique: 技术 (technology), 艺术 (art), 手术 (surgery), 魔术 (magic), 学术 (academic), 武术 (martial arts). It almost never stands alone.

examples.hanzi: 她学过一点魔术。
examples.pinyin: Tā xué guo yìdiǎn móshù.
examples.english: She has learned a little magic.

examples.hanzi: 这位艺术家很有名。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yìshùjiā hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: This artist is very famous.

components.note: 谷 (valley) — suggests an open gap, matching the sense of 'open, clear'; 豁 can also mean to exempt (豁免).
害 (hài) is only a loose sound hint for huò.
⺈ (bent figure) — top part, a person; with 口 and 儿 it forms 免. Origin unclear; Memory aid: a person with a hat slipping out, 'excused'.
儿 (legs) — the bottom part and radical, a walking person, as in 先 first and 兄 older brother.
木 (wood) — originally 權, the sliding weight of a steelyard scale: weighing, then power; 又 is just a simplification stand-in.

example.hanzi: 外交官享有法律豁免权。
example.pinyin: Wàijiāoguān xiǎngyǒu fǎlǜ huòmiǎnquán.
example.english: Diplomats enjoy legal immunity.
example.fact: Diplomatic immunity was formalized internationally by the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, but the underlying idea — that a foreign envoy should not be punished for the actions of the government they represent — is far older, with roots in customs observed by ancient Greek city-states to keep channels of communication open even between rivals.

examples.hanzi: 这位议员不享有豁免权。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yìyuán bù xiǎngyǒu huòmiǎnquán.
examples.english: This legislator does not have immunity.

examples.hanzi: 法院取消了他的豁免权。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn qǔxiāo le tā de huòmiǎnquán.
examples.english: The court revoked his immunity.

components.note: 世 (generation) — from 卅 (thirty): about thirty years is one generation, so an age or the world.

example.hanzi: 这是世界上最高的山。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì shìjiè shàng zuì gāo de shān.
example.english: This is the highest mountain in the world.
example.fact: 世 means a generation or lifetime: 世界 (world), 世纪 (century), 世代 (generations), 去世 (to pass away) and 一世 (a whole lifetime). The idea of 'three tens' in its shape is a commonly told explanation.

examples.hanzi: 他的祖父去世了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zǔfù qùshì le.
examples.english: His grandfather passed away.

examples.hanzi: 二十一世纪有很多新技术。
examples.pinyin: Èrshíyī shìjì yǒu hěn duō xīn jìshù.
examples.english: The 21st century has many new technologies.

components.note: 阝 (city, 右耳旁) — on the right it marks towns and places, as in 都 capital, 邦 nation; 郡 is a county.
君 (jūn) — close sound: 郡 jùn. 君 also sounds out 群 qún.

example.hanzi: 汉朝设置了许多郡。
example.pinyin: Hàncháo shèzhì le xǔduō jùn.
example.english: The Han dynasty set up many commanderies.
example.fact: 郡 was an administrative unit under the Qin and Han dynasties, above the 县 (county), forming the 郡县制 system. In Japan and Korea it survives as 'county' (gun).

examples.hanzi: 这座古城曾经是一个郡的中心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔchéng céngjīng shì yí ge jùn de zhōngxīn.
examples.english: This ancient city was once the center of a commandery.

examples.hanzi: 英国的约克郡风景很美。
examples.pinyin: Yīngguó de Yuēkè jùn fēngjǐng hěn měi.
examples.english: The scenery in Yorkshire, England, is beautiful.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; 草 is grass itself, as in 花 flower, 菜 vegetable.
早 (zǎo) shares the rhyme -ǎo with cǎo, a loose sound clue.

example.hanzi: 草地上有很多花。
example.pinyin: Cǎodì shàng yǒu hěn duō huā.
example.english: There are many flowers on the lawn.
example.fact: 草 builds 草地 (lawn), 草原 (grassland), 草莓 (strawberry) and 草稿 (rough draft). It can also mean careless: 草率 (hasty, sloppy).

examples.hanzi: 牛在草地上吃草。
examples.pinyin: Niú zài cǎodì shang chī cǎo.
examples.english: The cow is eating grass on the lawn.

examples.hanzi: 他对草莓过敏。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì cǎoméi guòmǐn.
examples.english: He is allergic to strawberries.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and meeting, as in 过, 进, 送; 遭 is to meet, usually with bad luck.
曹 (cáo) hints at the sound: 遭 zāo is close to 糟 zāo and 槽 cáo.

example.hanzi: 他遭到了拒绝。
example.pinyin: Tā zāodào le jùjué.
example.english: He was turned down.
example.fact: 遭 is for encountering something bad: 遭到 (to be subjected to), 遭遇 (to encounter), 遭殃 (to suffer disaster). It also counts trips: 走一遭 means to make a round trip.

examples.hanzi: 他在路上遭遇了一场大雨。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài lù shang zāoyù le yì chǎng dàyǔ.
examples.english: He was caught in a heavy rain on the road.

examples.hanzi: 村子遭受了严重的洪水。
examples.pinyin: Cūnzi zāoshòu le yánzhòng de hóngshuǐ.
examples.english: The village suffered a serious flood.

components.note: 广 (a roof on a wall) — buildings and rooms: 店 shop, 床 bed, 库 store, 度. Here also the simplified form of 廣, broad.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 播 is scattering seed by hand, then broadcasting.
番 (fān) — near sound — 播 is bō; 番 also sounds out 翻 fān and 潘 pān.

example.hanzi: 这个消息通过广播传遍了全国。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi tōngguò guǎngbō chuánbiànle quánguó.
example.english: This news spread across the whole country through the broadcast.
example.fact: Pittsburgh's KDKA is often credited with the first regularly scheduled commercial radio broadcast, airing results of the 1920 U.S. presidential election on the night of November 2. At the time, almost nobody owned a radio receiver, so the station is said to have loaned sets to listeners just to prove the new medium worked.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢在开车时听广播。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài kāichē shí tīng guǎngbō.
examples.english: I like listening to the radio while driving.

examples.hanzi: 电台正在广播天气预报。
examples.pinyin: Diàntái zhèngzài guǎngbō tiānqì yùbào.
examples.english: The radio station is broadcasting the weather forecast.

components.note: 西 (west) — traditionally a bird settling on its nest at sunset, hence west; 西 turns up in 要 and 栖.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — a blade 刂 cutting two jades apart: to divide into groups, hence class or shift.
牙 (tooth) — a picture of interlocking teeth; 牙 also sounds out 芽 yá and 讶 yà.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 语 is language and spoken words.
吾 (wú) — loose hint — 语 is yǔ; 吾 also sounds out 悟 wù.

example.hanzi: 她在大学学习西班牙语。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué xuéxí Xībānyáyǔ.
example.english: She studies Spanish at university.
example.fact: Spanish has more native speakers than English worldwide, ranking second only to Mandarin Chinese. It is an official language in 20 countries across four continents, a spread that traces back to Spanish colonial expansion beginning in the late 15th century.

examples.hanzi: 我的同学在学西班牙语。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tóngxué zài xué Xībānyáyǔ.
examples.english: My classmate is learning Spanish.

examples.hanzi: 你会说西班牙语吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì shuō Xībānyáyǔ ma?
examples.english: Can you speak Spanish?

components.note: 女 (woman) — traditional reading shows an axe-like weapon 戌 over a woman 女, hence power and authority; compare 姑 and 妈.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.
心 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 想, 怕, 思; 忌 is a feeling of jealousy or dread.
己 (jǐ) hints at the sound: 忌 jì is close, as in 记 jì and 纪 jì.

example.hanzi: 他喝了一杯威士忌。
example.pinyin: Tā hēle yì bēi wēishìjì.
example.english: He drank a glass of whiskey.
example.fact: Under Scottish law, a spirit can only be labeled 'Scotch whisky' if it has been aged in oak casks for at least three years, a rule that traces back to regulations tightened during the First World War to curb the sale of harsh, immature spirits. That legal minimum still shapes how distilleries plan production today.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢在冰块里加威士忌。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài bīngkuài lǐ jiā wēishìjì.
examples.english: He likes to add whiskey to ice.

examples.hanzi: 这瓶威士忌是朋友送的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè píng wēishìjì shì péngyou sòng de.
examples.english: This bottle of whiskey was a gift from a friend.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — the frame on the left and top, as in 原, 厚, 压. In 厌 it is just the old cliff-like frame of 厭.
犬 (quǎn, dog) — looks like a sound part but quǎn vs yàn is only a loose hint. The old 厭 got its sound from 猒 (yàn).
亻 (person) — marks people and states, as in 你, 休 rest; 倦 is a tired person.
卷 (juǎn) hints at the sound: 倦 juàn is close, as in 圈 juàn.

example.hanzi: 我对这份工作感到厌倦了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhè fèn gōngzuò gǎndào yànjuànle.
example.english: I've grown weary of this job.
example.fact: The World Health Organization formally added 'burnout' to its International Classification of Diseases in 2019, defining it as a syndrome from chronic, unmanaged workplace stress rather than a medical condition in itself. The classification was meant to help employers recognize it as an occupational issue, not a personal failing.

examples.hanzi: 天天吃同样的东西，我很厌倦。
examples.pinyin: Tiāntiān chī tóngyàng de dōngxi, wǒ hěn yànjuàn.
examples.english: I'm tired of eating the same thing every day.

examples.hanzi: 他从不厌倦学习新东西。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng bù yànjuàn xuéxí xīn dōngxi.
examples.english: He never gets tired of learning new things.

components.note: 缶 (earthenware jar) — pottery vessels, as in 缸 vat, 缺 lack.
雚 (guàn) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 灌 guàn.

example.hanzi: 桌子上有一罐可乐。
example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yí guàn kělè.
example.english: There is a can of cola on the table.
example.fact: 罐 is both a container and a measure word: 罐头 (canned food), 易拉罐 (pull-tab can), 茶叶罐 (tea caddy). 拔罐 is cupping, a traditional therapy using heated glass cups.

examples.hanzi: 我买了一罐茶叶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yí guàn cháyè.
examples.english: I bought a can of tea leaves.

examples.hanzi: 他把糖放进了罐子里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ táng fàng jìn le guànzi li.
examples.english: He put the sugar into the jar.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
聲 (traditional) — a hanging stone chime struck, with 耳 (ear) below: a sound you hear. 声 keeps only the top, so the picture is mostly lost.
士 (scholar) — the top of 声 is only a leftover of the old chime, not 'scholar'. Do not read meaning into it.

example.hanzi: 他大声地喊了他的名字。
example.pinyin: Tā dàshēng de hǎnle tā de míngzì.
example.english: He shouted his name loudly.
example.fact: The 1883 eruption of the volcano Krakatoa is often called the loudest sound in recorded history — it was reportedly heard nearly 3,000 miles away in Rodrigues Island, and sailors 40 miles from the blast had their eardrums ruptured by the pressure wave.

examples.hanzi: 请大声一点，我听不清楚。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàshēng yìdiǎn, wǒ tīng bù qīngchu.
examples.english: Please speak louder, I can't hear clearly.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们大声唱起歌来。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen dàshēng chàng qǐ gē lái.
examples.english: The children started singing loudly.

components.note: 大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.

example.hanzi: 今天的天空非常蓝。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān de tiānkōng fēicháng lán.
example.english: Today's sky is very blue.
example.fact: The sky looks blue because Earth's atmosphere scatters shorter blue wavelengths of sunlight far more than longer red wavelengths, a phenomenon known as Rayleigh scattering. On Mars, where the atmosphere is thin and dusty, the effect works differently and the daytime sky often appears butterscotch or reddish instead.

examples.hanzi: 天空中飘着几朵白云。
examples.pinyin: Tiānkōng zhōng piāo zhe jǐ duǒ báiyún.
examples.english: A few white clouds are drifting in the sky.

examples.hanzi: 夜晚的天空里有很多星星。
examples.pinyin: Yèwǎn de tiānkōng lǐ yǒu hěn duō xīngxing.
examples.english: There are many stars in the night sky.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅只使用本地食材。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng zhǐ shǐyòng běndì shícái.
example.english: This restaurant only uses local ingredients.
example.fact: The word 'locavore,' describing someone who tries to eat only food grown near where they live, was coined in 2005 by a small group of writers in the San Francisco Bay Area and was later named Oxford Word of the Year in 2007.

examples.hanzi: 你是本地人吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì běndì rén ma?
examples.english: Are you a local?

examples.hanzi: 我们想尝尝本地的特色菜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiǎng chángchang běndì de tèsè cài.
examples.english: We'd like to try the local specialties.

components.note: 米 (rice) — marks grain and rice, as in 粥 congee, 糖 sugar; 粘 is sticky, like cooked rice.
占 (zhàn) — close sound: 粘 zhān/nián. 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 沾 zhān.

example.hanzi: 请用胶水把纸粘上。
example.pinyin: Qǐng yòng jiāoshuǐ bǎ zhǐ zhān shàng.
example.english: Please stick the paper on with glue.
example.fact: 粘 is the verb 'to stick': 粘贴 (paste, as in 复制粘贴 copy and paste), 粘住 (to stick to). Read nián, it is a variant of 黏 for 'sticky'. It is also a surname, Niàn.

examples.hanzi: 这种胶带粘得很牢。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng jiāodài zhān de hěn láo.
examples.english: This tape sticks very firmly.

examples.hanzi: 他把照片粘在本子上。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhàopiàn zhān zài běnzi shang.
examples.english: He glued the photo into the notebook.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 妙 first meant fine and delicate.
少 (shǎo) — loose hint — 妙 is miào; 少 also means few or little.

example.hanzi: 这个主意真妙!
example.pinyin: Zhège zhǔyi zhēn miào!
example.english: What a brilliant idea!
example.fact: 妙 means wonderful or ingenious: 奇妙 (marvelous), 美妙 (beautiful), 巧妙 (clever), 妙招 (a clever trick). 不妙 means 'not good' and 莫名其妙 means baffling.

examples.hanzi: 这个办法真巧妙。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ zhēn qiǎomiào.
examples.english: This method is really clever.

examples.hanzi: 他的回答妙极了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huídá miào jí le.
examples.english: His answer was brilliant.

components.note: 冫 (ice, two drops) — marks cold and freezing, as in 冷 cold, 冻 freeze, 凉 cool; 冰 is 冫 plus 水 water: frozen water.
⺮ (bamboo) — 竹 (bamboo) as in 笔, 筷, 篮; boxes and baskets were woven from bamboo, so 箱 is a box or chest.
相 (xiāng) — same sound — 箱 is xiāng, just like 相.

example.hanzi: 牛奶放在冰箱里。
example.pinyin: Niúnǎi fàngzài bīngxiāng lǐ.
example.english: The milk is in the refrigerator.
example.fact: Household refrigerators were a rarity for decades after their invention; even in the United States, fewer than 10% of homes owned one in 1930, and it took mass production through the 1930s and '40s to make them a standard kitchen appliance.

examples.hanzi: 冰箱坏了，需要修理。
examples.pinyin: Bīngxiāng huài le, xūyào xiūlǐ.
examples.english: The refrigerator is broken and needs repair.

examples.hanzi: 请把剩菜放进冰箱。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shèngcài fàng jìn bīngxiāng.
examples.english: Please put the leftovers in the fridge.

meanings: Long live (the king, the revolution etc)!

components.note: 萬 (traditional ten thousand) — 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which pictured a scorpion borrowed for the number 10,000; 万 also sounds out 迈 mài.
山 (mountain) — the top part and radical, as in 岛 island. 岁 is simplified from 歲; Memory aid: a mountain of evenings (夕) passing makes years, 万岁 'long live'.
夕 (evening) — the bottom part, as in 外 and 多. It stands for passing time, so a year is many evenings; memory aid.

example.hanzi: 人群高呼国王万岁。
example.pinyin: Rénqún gāohū guówáng wànsuì.
example.english: The crowd shouted 'long live the king.'
example.fact: Louis XIV of France holds the record for the longest verified reign of any monarch in history: 72 years and 110 days, having become king in 1643 at the age of four and ruling until his death in 1715.

examples.hanzi: 祝你生日快乐，万岁！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēngrì kuàilè, wànsuì!
examples.english: Happy birthday, hooray!

examples.hanzi: 古代的人们常喊皇帝万岁。
examples.pinyin: Gǔdài de rénmen cháng hǎn huángdì wànsuì.
examples.english: People in ancient times often shouted "long live the emperor."

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; sand grains are tiny bits washed by water.
少 (shǎo) — near sound — 沙 is shā; 少 also sounds out 炒 chǎo and 纱 shā.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在沙滩上玩沙子。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài shātān shàng wán shāzi.
example.english: The children are playing in the sand on the beach.
example.fact: 沙 builds 沙子 (sand), 沙滩 (beach) and 沙漠 (desert). It also stands in for sounds: 沙发 (sofa) and 沙拉 (salad). Describing a voice as 沙哑 means hoarse.

examples.hanzi: 他的嗓子有点沙哑。
examples.pinyin: Tā de sǎngzi yǒudiǎn shāyǎ.
examples.english: His voice is a bit hoarse.

examples.hanzi: 我们在沙发上看电视。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài shāfā shang kàn diànshì.
examples.english: We watch TV on the sofa.

meanings: partner (in a business or other joint venture)

components.note: 合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 伙 is a companion.
火 (huǒ, fire) gives the exact sound; 火 also means fire.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 他们是律师事务所的合伙人。
example.pinyin: Tāmen shì lǜshī shìwùsuǒ de héhuǒrén.
example.english: They are partners at the law firm.
example.fact: Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger ran Berkshire Hathaway together for more than five decades, a partnership widely regarded as one of the longest and most successful in modern corporate history, until Munger's death in 2023 at age 99.

examples.hanzi: 我想找一个合伙人一起开店。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zhǎo yí ge héhuǒrén yìqǐ kāi diàn.
examples.english: I want to find a partner to open a shop together.

examples.hanzi: 他的合伙人负责管理账目。
examples.pinyin: Tā de héhuǒrén fùzé guǎnlǐ zhàngmù.
examples.english: His partner is in charge of managing the accounts.

components.note: 见 (see) — seeing and looking, as in 现, 觉, 看: 视 is to look.
礻 here is 示 (shì), the altar radical in 礼 and 神: in 视 it is the exact sound clue.
页 (head) — marks the head and face, as in 顶 top, 题 topic, 额 forehead; 频 pairs it with repeating motion for 'again and again'.

example.hanzi: 这个视频已经有一百万次观看。
example.pinyin: Zhège shìpín yǐjīng yǒu yìbǎiwàn cì guānkàn.
example.english: This video already has a million views.
example.fact: The first video ever uploaded to YouTube, a 19-second clip titled 'Me at the zoo,' was posted by co-founder Jawed Karim on April 23, 2005. It shows him standing in front of the elephant enclosure at the San Diego Zoo and is still viewable on the site today.

examples.hanzi: 我昨晚看了一个有趣的视频。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn kàn le yí ge yǒuqù de shìpín.
examples.english: I watched an interesting video last night.

examples.hanzi: 我们晚上用视频聊天吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshang yòng shìpín liáotiān ba.
examples.english: Let's video chat tonight.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — written things and bamboo goods: 笔 pen, 第 order, 筷 chopsticks; 答 comes from bamboo slips used for replies.
合 (hé, together) — matching an answer to a question; sound is only loose, but 合 also sounds out 搭 dā.

example.hanzi: 请回答这个问题。
example.pinyin: Qǐng huídá zhège wèntí.
example.english: Please answer this question.
example.fact: 答 is read dá for answering: 回答 (answer), 答案 (answer key), 答题 (to answer questions). In 答应, 'to agree, promise', it is read dā, a classic reading pitfall.

examples.hanzi: 老师在等你的答案。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī zài děng nǐ de dá'àn.
examples.english: The teacher is waiting for your answer.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你的答复。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ de dáfù.
examples.english: Thank you for your reply.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — liquids and flow: 河, 汤, 酒; 治 first meant controlling water, then governing and curing.
台 (tái) is only a loose sound hint; the same part is in 始 shǐ and 胎 tāi.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.

example.hanzi: 这个城市的治安一直很好。
example.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de zhì'ān yìzhí hěn hǎo.
example.english: This city's public order has always been good.
example.fact: London's Metropolitan Police, established by Sir Robert Peel in 1829, is widely considered the model for modern civilian policing. Its officers are still nicknamed 'bobbies' after Peel, and the force's founding principle — policing by consent rather than force — influenced police departments around the world.

examples.hanzi: 这个小区的治安很不错。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎoqū de zhì'ān hěn búcuò.
examples.english: The public security in this neighborhood is quite good.

examples.hanzi: 警察负责维护社区治安。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá fùzé wéihù shèqū zhì'ān.
examples.english: The police are responsible for maintaining public order in the community.

components.note: 穴 (hole, cave) — 穴 is a hole, as in 空, 窗, 突; 穿 is to pierce through, and the 牙 is a tooth boring in.
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.

example.hanzi: 她的穿着总是很整洁。
example.pinyin: Tā de chuānzhuó zǒngshì hěn zhěngjié.
example.english: Her attire is always neat.
example.fact: Buttons have existed as decorative objects for over 5,000 years, but they weren't widely used as functional fasteners until buttonholes were invented in Europe around the 13th century — an innovation that also made tightly fitted clothing possible for the first time.

examples.hanzi: 天冷了，你要注意穿着。
examples.pinyin: Tiān lěng le, nǐ yào zhùyì chuānzhuó.
examples.english: It's getting cold, so you should pay attention to what you wear.

examples.hanzi: 面试时的穿着很重要。
examples.pinyin: Miànshì shí de chuānzhuó hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: What you wear to an interview is very important.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
买 (mǎi, buy) — its sound is almost the same as 卖 mài, and the meaning is the opposite: buy and sell.

example.hanzi: 他为了钱出卖了朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā wèile qián chūmàile péngyǒu.
example.english: He betrayed his friend for money.
example.fact: CIA officer Aldrich Ames sold classified information to the Soviet Union and later Russia for nearly a decade before his arrest in 1994, in one of the most damaging espionage cases in U.S. history. His disclosures are believed to have led to the deaths of at least ten American intelligence sources.

examples.hanzi: 他们出卖了公司的秘密。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen chūmài le gōngsī de mìmì.
examples.english: They sold out the company's secrets.

examples.hanzi: 我永远不会出卖你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒngyuǎn bú huì chūmài nǐ.
examples.english: I will never betray you.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 标 first meant the tip of a tree, hence a mark or target; wood radical as in 树 tree, 板 board.
票 (piào) is the sound in traditional 標; same series 漂 piāo and 飘 piāo; simplified 标 now shows 示.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.

example.hanzi: 请在地图上标记你的位置。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài dìtú shàng biāojì nǐ de wèizhi.
example.english: Please mark your location on the map.
example.fact: The Latin phrase 'hic sunt dracones' ('here be dragons'), often imagined as a common warning on old maps, actually appears on only one known historical map — the 1510 Hunt-Lenox Globe, one of the oldest surviving globes to depict the New World.

examples.hanzi: 老师用红笔标记了重点。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī yòng hóngbǐ biāojì le zhòngdiǎn.
examples.english: The teacher marked the key points with a red pen.

examples.hanzi: 这封邮件被标记为重要。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fēng yóujiàn bèi biāojì wéi zhòngyào.
examples.english: This email has been marked as important.

components.note: 玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.

example.hanzi: 游泳可以锻炼全身的肌肉。
example.pinyin: Yóuyǒng kěyǐ duànliàn quánshēn de jīròu.
example.english: Swimming can exercise the muscles of the whole body.
example.fact: Skeletal muscle makes up roughly 40% of an average adult's total body mass, more than any other single tissue type in the human body, including bone, fat, or organs.

examples.hanzi: 我跑完步后全身都是汗。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ pǎo wán bù hòu quánshēn dōu shì hàn.
examples.english: After running, I was sweating all over.

examples.hanzi: 他全身都湿透了。
examples.pinyin: Tā quánshēn dōu shītòu le.
examples.english: He was soaked all over.

meanings: dedicated (to a particular field or purpose)

components.note: 专 (zhuān) also gives its sound to 转 zhuǎn, 传 chuán, 砖 zhuān and 团 tuán (traditional 專).
门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.hanzi: 这个实验室专门研究癌症治疗。
example.pinyin: Zhège shíyànshì zhuānmén yánjiū áizhèng zhìliáo.
example.english: This laboratory specializes in cancer treatment research.
example.fact: The first effective chemotherapy drug, nitrogen mustard, emerged from an unexpected observation: doctors noticed that soldiers exposed to mustard gas in World War II had unusually low white blood cell counts. That insight led researchers in the 1940s to test related compounds against lymphoma, launching the modern era of cancer chemotherapy.

examples.hanzi: 他是专门来看你的。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zhuānmén lái kàn nǐ de.
examples.english: He came especially to see you.

examples.hanzi: 这家店专门卖手工面包。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn zhuānmén mài shǒugōng miànbāo.
examples.english: This shop specializes in handmade bread.

components.note: 夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.
禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 科 first meant grading grain with a measure 斗, and then categories like 科学.
斗 (dipper) — 斗 is a measuring dipper, as in 斗 (a unit of grain).

example.hanzi: 他的父亲是一名外科医生。
example.pinyin: Tā de fùqīn shì yì míng wàikē yīshēng.
example.english: His father is a surgeon.
example.fact: Ether was first used publicly as a surgical anesthetic on October 16, 1846, at Massachusetts General Hospital, in an operation now commemorated annually as 'Ether Day.' Before that demonstration, surgery meant enduring the operation fully conscious, so the discovery transformed what procedures were even possible.

examples.hanzi: 她在医院的外科工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yīyuàn de wàikē gōngzuò.
examples.english: She works in the surgery department of the hospital.

examples.hanzi: 他需要去外科做检查。
examples.pinyin: Tā xūyào qù wàikē zuò jiǎnchá.
examples.english: He needs to go to the surgery department for an examination.
